audiences.executive: Leave the current platform on your own timeline, with each application owner signing off its move, and come out with a better service, not just a new platform.
audiences.technical: Moves in waves, each with a runbook, a rollback and a check against a baseline; policies applied as machines arrive; addresses kept.
audiences.financial: The cost of change weighed against the next renewal and the hardware that can stay; the return is in what runs better afterwards, not only in licences.

people: The sponsor who owns the decision and the renewal date
Application owners, who sign off each move
Change management and the service desk
Finance, for the renewal and the hardware still being paid for

objections.says: A migration is a risk we cannot take this year.
objections.clarify: Which applications carry the risk, and what does staying through the next renewal cost?
objections.answer: Start with the wave that teaches the most for the least risk, with a rollback written before anything moves.
objections.prove: Move a test wave with its runbook, and roll one machine back on purpose.

objections.says: It changes nothing for the business: the same machines on another platform.
objections.clarify: What would be visibly better for users or the business after the move?
objections.answer: Tie each wave to an improvement people can see: protection on arrival, self-service, faster changes, updates in working hours.
objections.prove: Show one visible improvement working on the migrated test wave, signed off by its owner.

objections.says: We cannot change IP addresses or our tools.
objections.clarify: Which tools must keep working (backup, monitoring, security), and which addresses are written into applications?
objections.answer: Keep the addresses and integrate the tools that stay; re-addressing is not a condition of the move.
objections.prove: Migrate test machines without changing their addresses, and see them in the current monitoring and backup tools.

objections.says: Our team has no time to run a migration.
objections.clarify: Who would do the work today, and in which change windows?
objections.answer: Plan waves that fit the windows, automate the repetitive steps, and agree who does what among the customer, a partner and us.
objections.prove: Time a test wave end to end and build the plan from that time, not from estimates.
